video_title: Doug Christie reveals Keegan Murray was sick in Kings’ loss | NBC Sports California

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie praises Kings' competitive effort despite loss
quotes.excerpt: I was proud of the guys stepping up. It was a lot going on, and I thought they stepped up and they competed.
quotes.quote: I was proud of the guys stepping up. It was a lot going on, and I thought they stepped up and they competed. You are asking a lot out of guys, and in those moments, execution is big. We got to execute better. Some of them guys were put in those positions, and I thought they did a marvelous job of getting down a little bit, coming back, and competing. But at the end of quarters and the end of halves, that is where games are won, especially against an incredible player in Shai and a really, really good sound team defense.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie says he was proud of the Kings for competing despite a difficult situation and a tough loss to a sound defensive team in OKC.

structured.context: Kings assistant coach Doug Christie discusses the team's performance and execution in a loss against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie emphasizes execution and defensive discipline
quotes.excerpt: I think the biggest takeaway probably is the execution piece.
quotes.quote: I think more than anything, it is like you are capable of doing a lot, because a lot was thrown at them right before the game, and nobody blinked. Everybody said, 'Let's go,' as a unit, as a team. I think the biggest takeaway probably is the execution piece. Part of it was you got to make sure that because their shell is so tight on the defensive end, when you come off of a pick and roll, when you gain an advantage and you see a player in front of you, you got to get off of it right away because they are going to collapse and not allow you to drive those lanes.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on the Kings offensive struggles against the Thunder shell defense: When you gain an advantage you have to get off the ball right away because they are going to collapse.

structured.context: Doug Christie explains the tactical challenges of facing the Thunder's defensive scheme.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie discusses the challenge of playing without starters
quotes.excerpt: This is big boy basketball and that is the nature of the beast.
quotes.quote: You learn early that we walked through, had a plan, everything, and then all that just happens and you just got to scrap and throw it out the window. But this is big boy basketball and that is the nature of the beast. Nobody is going to check for you, no one cares. You got to step up, and that is where I was proud of them. I thought that they came back. I threw a lot at them tonight. We were changing defenses on the fly multiple times, trying to show Shai different looks, their team different looks, and I thought they executed it.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on the challenge of adjusting the game plan on the fly: This is big boy basketball and that is the nature of the beast. Nobody is going to check for you.

structured.context: Doug Christie reflects on the team's ability to adjust defensive strategies on the fly against Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie confirms Keegan Murray was playing while sick
quotes.excerpt: Keegan did not feel well, and he gave us everything that he had.
quotes.quote: Keegan did not feel well, and he gave us everything that he had, and that is a massive amount of respect for the kid because he is like, 'I am just going to figure it out.' I am seeing him hydrating, and I am looking at him, and I am like, 'You need one?' No. But the way he said no was like, 'Get in there and get him, get him over a break, put him back in.' But the guys who played, they played their hearts out.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie reveals Keegan Murray was playing while sick against the Thunder: He gave us everything that he had and that is a massive amount of respect for the kid.

structured.context: Doug Christie reveals that Keegan Murray played through an illness during the game.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie commends Lyles and Davion Mitchell's physicality
quotes.excerpt: I thought the energy, the physicality of the game, I thought they met both of those head on.
quotes.quote: I thought the energy, the physicality of the game, I thought they met both of those head on. You are asking both of those guys to guard the MVP, and you are trying to keep your hand out of the cookie jar. The physicality, there were some rebounds, some tips, some running the floor, shooting the basketball. A little while ago it was like, 'Hey, you are in. No problem, here I go.' That just speaks to their preparation, their professionalism, and their willingness to do whatever is asked of them. I have a massive amount of respect for how they go about their business.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie praises the professionalism of Trey Lyles and Davion Mitchell for stepping up and meeting the physicality of the game head on.

structured.context: Doug Christie praises the professionalism and physicality of Trey Lyles and Davion Mitchell.
